info.description: Economics is the study of how the society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While macroeconomics studies aggregate issues related to national and international economic activities, this course - microeconomics - focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents. Microeconomics studies how households (or individuals), business (or firms, enterprises) and the government make decisions, given scarcity of resources. It also studies the interactions among those market members and how these interactions have impacts on their economic benefits and the economy. Because most of these activities occur in the markets, this course also focuses on how the markets work.
info.studentTasks:
+ Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

+ Read textbooks and other materials in advance before class

+ Actively participate in class activities

+ Complete all homework assignments and other tasks given by the instructor

+ Use personal laptop in class only for learning purposes

+ Don’t have private conversations or arrive at class late, which can disrupt the learning environment of the class

clos.loDetails: Explain why consumers attempt to maximize utility.
Shows self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context
Describe long runs and short runs
Discuss fixed, variable, and total costs
Identify the characteristics of microeconomics and its effect consumers, businesses, and owners
Recognize the three primary forms of elasticity as their impacts on economics
Review curve analysis and how it reflects consumer demand
Apply utility theory to the changing world of supply and demand
Describe cost curves and consumer variables
Recognize the role of supply and demand in economics, government policies.
